review.summary: The main theorem, dependency chain, numerical artifacts and PDF check out. One change to an archived auxiliary statement remains without recorded authorization.
issues: manuscript/sections/02-preliminaries.tex:87–91, changes.md §4 item 19 and §10, and sections/B-provenance.tex:25: Lemma 2.6 replaces the archived infinite-interval identity by convergence of the sum–integral difference, with the identity conditional on separate convergence. This formulation is correct, but retaining the hypotheses does not preserve the original conclusion’s strength. No supplied intervention authorizes this change. Obtain and record Markus’s decision on the presentation before treating it as accepted. Both archived applications converge absolutely, so this is not a load-bearing gap in P5 or the main theorem.
review.statement_checks: Compared P1–P9 statements and proofs with the manuscript. The polynomial class, derivative weight, real-variable hypotheses, ranges, quantifiers, uniformity and three final error terms are preserved. The exponent min(δ/12,1/(6d)) follows from the displayed ratios. Explicit constants and the broader P6 range are supported by archived proofs. The P1 normalization/convergence corrections, P3 factor-of-two calculation and P8 endpoint treatment work. Lemma 2.6 is mathematically correct in its present form, subject to the authorization issue above. No brief.md was supplied.
review.dependency_checks: Independently checked the merged tail, residue-count and coprime-pair arguments; the exact cancellation in P2; uniform Möbius truncation in P3; P4’s convergent divisor-error sum; and P5’s Euler–Maclaurin boundary terms and convolution. The five sawtooth bounds total 449Λ/8 < 57Λ, preserving c₁=60. P8 handles repeated factors and content primes using ρ(p²)≤pρ(p), with valid truncation and residue-class errors. P7 and P9 invoke dependencies within their contracts and absorb ε correctly. No load-bearing source gap found.
review.numerics_checks: Inspected reproduce.py, accepted compute.py/counts.cpp, reproduction.json and reproduce.log. The computation recompiles and reruns accepted code; tables are not merely transcribed archived values. All accepted numerical artifact hashes match. Independently refitted the archived rows, recomputed the Euler products, root checks, identity self-test and all 66 exact-shape rows, and regenerated all 27 generated artifacts in memory: every artifact matched. Direct residue counting reproduced all 16 quadratic/cubic rows at x=250000 with maximum relative variance discrepancy 6.7e-16. The identity self-test gave 4.7831e-10. Fit envelopes, outward rounding, prime-tail bounds and finite-range limitations are represented accurately. The full C++ NTT grid was not rerun during this read-only review; its supplied execution evidence and code path were audited. Floating-point product intervals remain uncertified, as disclosed.
review.citation_checks: Checked the cited mathematical inputs and background against supplied PDFs: R. C. Vaughan, A variance for k-free numbers in arithmetic progressions (2005), https://doi.org/10.1112/S0024611505015352; H. L. Montgomery and R. C. Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I. Classical Theory (2007), https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511618314, Theorems 1.8/1.9/1.12, (2.20), and Corollary 10.4. Also checked J. Brüdern et al., On the exponential sum over k-free numbers (1998), and J. Brüdern–T. D. Wooley, Sparse variance for primes in arithmetic progression (2011); their locators are unavailable in the supplied material, explicitly disclosed. BW’s attribution to D. A. Goldston–R. C. Vaughan, On the Montgomery–Hooley asymptotic formula (1997), https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511526091.010, and R. C. Vaughan, On a variance associated with the distribution of general sequences in arithmetic progressions. I (1998), https://doi.org/10.1098/rsta.1998.0185, is supported. Appendix B of Montgomery–Vaughan is unavailable; the needed formula is proved directly. No online research or excluded source was used.
review.provenance_checks: Appendix B agrees with provenance.json on repository, archive commit, recorded revision, models, roles and CLI versions; unavailable model-weight versions remain unknown. No human authorship is claimed. All nine proof hashes match the recorded values, and the supplied passing reviews identify those proofs. Generated-artifact and PDF hashes match build-inputs.json. Contract/approval digest serialization and the opaque accepted_snapshot digest could not be independently reconstructed. Earlier write-up review history cannot be authenticated because those reports are absent; none was consulted. The archived acceptance does not authorize the later Lemma 2.6 change.
review.layout_checks: Used Poppler pdfinfo and pdftotext -layout, and visually inspected rendered pages 3, 4, 6, 7, 14, 15, 20, 21, 24–30 and 32. The 32-page PDF is complete and readable. Checked theorem inequalities, dense equations, all eight tables, all three figures, legends, bibliography and provenance text. No clipping, collisions, missing symbols or unresolved references were found. The build logs show no overfull boxes or undefined references; visual inspection supports that result.
